title: OpenTitan counter: a real security block
what: prim_count from OpenTitan, an open-source security chip. It keeps every count twice, one copy counting up and one counting down, and raises err_o when they disagree.
why: Counters limit retries and prove that steps ran. A glitch that changes a count without anyone noticing can skip a limit.
teaches: A real industrial protection, checked by the same question. The plain counter falls to one glitch; OpenTitan's cross counter needs two (one on the counter, one on the error check).
lesson_after: The cross counter doubles the cost: the attacker must change the count and also silence the error check. Note the answer is bounded (5 cycles); the proof section says whether it also holds for any waiting time.
